Perfect Liv is a classical Ayurvedic hepatoprotective formulation built for maintenance support and for the phase after a liver insult, when enzymes are elevated and the organ needs help recovering.

It is a very safe and effective herbal formula that helps protect a patient's liver suffering from viral hepatitis, drug-induced hepatotoxicity, alcohol-induced hepatotoxicity and cholestatic jaundice.

It is presented simply, without exotic claims: reduces SGPT, SGOT and bilirubin, increases bile flow, improves liver immunity, and reverses hepatic cell damage.
safety_info: If you have been diagnosed with a liver condition, use only under medical supervision — this supports treatment, it does not replace it. Not a substitute for prescribed antiviral or specialist therapy in hepatitis. Not for children except on medical advice.

directions: Adults: 15 ml (one tablespoonful) once or twice daily after meals. Children: as directed by your physician. Take with a source of vitamin C such as citrus juice to aid absorption; avoid taking with tea, coffee or calcium supplements, which reduce it.
composition: Each 15 ml (one tablespoonful) contains: Ferric Ammonium Citrate IP 160 mg (equivalent to Elemental Iron 32.8 mg), Cyanocobalamin IP 7.5 mcg, Folic Acid IP 0.5 mg, Alcohol (95%) 0.87 ml (as Ethyl Alcohol).
description:
Iron deficiency is the most common nutritional deficiency in India, and the most commonly abandoned supplement — because ferrous salts cause constipation, nausea and a metallic taste that most people will not tolerate for the three to six months a correction actually takes.

Haemerange uses Ferric Ammonium Citrate, which is generally better tolerated than plain ferrous sulphate, and pairs it with folic acid and cyanocobalamin so that all three inputs to red cell production are covered together. Each 15 ml tablespoonful provides 160 mg of ferric ammonium citrate, equivalent to 32.8 mg of elemental iron, with 7.5 mcg of B12 and 0.5 mg of folic acid.

It is orange flavoured for the same reason it is a syrup: the dose that gets taken is the only one that raises a haemoglobin count.
safety_info: Contains 0.87 ml alcohol (95%) per 15 ml. Iron overdose is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under six — keep well out of reach. Do not take alongside another iron supplement. Iron may darken the stool, which is harmless. Consult your doctor before use if you have haemochromatosis or any iron-overload condition.

directions: Take 1 capsule daily after a meal with water, or as directed by your healthcare practitioner. Do not take at the same time as an iron supplement or thyroid medication — space them at least two hours apart.
composition: Each soft gelatin capsule contains: Calcium Carbonate IP 500 mg, Calcitriol IP 0.25 mcg, Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate IP equivalent to Elemental Zinc 7.5 mg, Magnesium Sulphate IP equivalent to Elemental Magnesium 50 mg, Vitamin K27 45 mcg, Methylcobalamin IP 1500 mcg, L-Methyl Folate 800 mcg, Excipients q.s.
description:
Taking calcium on its own is close to pointless. Calcium needs calcitriol — the active form of vitamin D — to be absorbed from the gut, and it needs Vitamin K to be directed into bone rather than deposited in soft tissue and arteries. Magnesium is required for the enzymes that handle it. Miss those and most of a calcium tablet simply passes through.

Calcin-K27 is built around that dependency chain. Each soft gelatin capsule carries 500 mg of calcium carbonate with calcitriol 0.25 mcg, Vitamin K27 45 mcg, elemental magnesium 50 mg and elemental zinc 7.5 mg, plus methylcobalamin 1500 mcg and L-methyl folate 800 mcg for nerve and homocysteine support.

The softgel format matters too: a liquid-filled capsule disperses faster than a compressed chalk tablet and avoids the constipation that makes people abandon calcium supplements.
safety_info: Consult your doctor before use if you have kidney stones, hypercalcaemia, or kidney disease, or if you take digoxin, thiazide diuretics or thyroid medication. Contains calcitriol — do not combine with another active vitamin D analogue without medical supervision. Not for children except on medical advice.
